title: Client-Side-Only Lease Validation
pattern: Checking a local lease's temporal expiration status (e.g., using `Instant::now()` vs. `valid_until`) to gate execution of an exclusive task, under the assumption that the time between the validation check and task completion is negligible or zero.
why_bad: It assumes instantaneous execution, ignoring that local processes can pause for several seconds due to GC, operating system kernel interrupts, swapping, or CPU frequency throttling [14, 23, 158]. Gating state mutation on client-side time checks alone cannot prevent operations from executing after the lease has expired, violating mutual exclusion invariants [158, 159].
detection: Identify `if` conditions that query methods returning temporal lease validity status immediately prior to executing blocks containing side-effects or network calls, without intervening synchronization or server-side token checks.
fix: Never rely on temporal local checks for mutual exclusion safety. Structure the lease system around logical tokens or validate lease correctness atomically on the target server with each execution step [91, 159, 164].
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 8 / passages [14, 158, 159]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 14 / passage [82]; Heather Adkins et al., *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, Chapter 14 / passage [91].
